newsitem.title: ITALY: Salomon reaffirms buy on Italy's SanPaolo.
newsitem.headline: Salomon reaffirms buy on Italy's SanPaolo.

text.p: U.S. investment house Salomon Brothers said it reaffirmed its buy recommendation on Italian bank San Paolo, regarding the Turin group as well positioned to deal with expected consolidation in Italy's banking sector.
"We consider San Paolo attractive among Italian banks for both its franchise and management discipline and reaffirm our buy recommendation," a Salomon research note said.

"San Paolo has implemented programmes to improve asset quality and boost its return on equity to the 10 percent range by 1999. We consider this goal realistic in view of the growing economy," it said.
Salomon said it expected San Paolo to be the first of the major foundation-controlled Italian banks to complete the transition to private sector ownership.
"The strength of its capital and franchise positions San Paolo well to benefit from the consolidation we expect in Italian banking as this process unfolds," it said.

"Although profitibility remains low in Italian banking, Italy's tighter fiscal stance and improving inflation picture promise gradual improvement in the operating environment for banks along with higher valuations for bank shares," Salomon said.
